evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The manager_restarted predicate only proves that the manager PID and invocation ID differ between the before/after snapshots. A guest reboot between those snapshots also changes both values, so it can satisfy this check without the manager-restart step being isolated; the separate boot_id_changed predicate applies only to the planned reboot pair. Requiring nonempty equal boot IDs in the manager snapshot pair is a correctness repair for the existing manager-restarted claim, while retaining the PID and invocation-ID checks so an unchanged manager on the same boot does not pass.
